35016: Who was Moses' father-in-law, described as the priest of Midian?
35017: Jethro (also called Reuel) was priest of Midian; he later advised Moses to appoint judges to share the work.
35018: Which woman was judging Israel while sitting under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel?
35019: Deborah, a prophet, judged Israel and summoned Barak against Sisera. Jael killed Sisera, but she was not a judge.
35020: Who was the mother of the prophet Samuel?
35021: Hannah prayed for a son at Shiloh and dedicated Samuel to the LORD. Peninnah was her husband's other wife.
35022: Ruth the Moabite was the great-grandmother of which king?
35023: Ruth and Boaz had Obed, Obed was the father of Jesse, and Jesse was the father of David.
35024: Who resolved to approach the king uninvited, saying "if I perish, I perish"?
35025: Esther agreed to go to King Ahasuerus without being summoned, which could mean death, after asking the Jews of Susa to fast for her.
35026: Which prisoner did Pilate release at the crowd's demand instead of Jesus?
35028: Pilate customarily released a prisoner at the feast; the crowd chose Barabbas. Simon of Cyrene carried Jesus' cross; Malchus was the high priest's servant whose ear was cut off.
35029: Which chief tax collector climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus?
35030: Zacchaeus of Jericho was short, so he climbed a sycamore; Jesus invited himself to his house.
35031: Who is the first follower of Jesus whose martyrdom Acts records?
35032: Stephen was stoned after his speech to the council (Acts 7). James son of Zebedee was killed later by Herod Agrippa I (Acts 12).
35033: Peter raised which disciple, known for good works and charity, from the dead in Joppa?
35036: Tabitha, called Dorcas in Greek, was raised in Joppa. Aeneas was a paralysed man Peter healed in Lydda; Eutychus was revived by Paul in Troas.
35037: Which young man fell asleep and fell from a third-storey window during Paul's long talk at Troas?
35038: Eutychus fell and was taken up dead, but Paul embraced him and said his life was in him.
35040: Leah bore Reuben first. He later lost the privileges of the firstborn because he slept with Bilhah, his father's concubine.
35041: Which of Abraham's relatives chose the Jordan plain and settled near Sodom?
35046: When their herds became too large, Lot chose the well-watered Jordan valley and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
35047: Which disciple of Jesus is also called Didymus, meaning "Twin"?
35048: John's Gospel three times calls Thomas "Didymus."
35049: Who was the king of Salem and priest of God Most High who blessed Abram?
35051: Melchizedek brought bread and wine and blessed Abram, who gave him a tenth. Hebrews links Jesus' priesthood to his.
35052: Who took Apollos aside in Ephesus and explained the way of God to him more accurately?
35057: Apollos knew only the baptism of John; Priscilla and Aquila taught him more fully.
35059: In which village did Jesus perform his first sign, turning water into wine?
35062: John calls the wedding miracle at Cana in Galilee the first of Jesus' signs.
35063: Where did Elijah challenge the prophets of Baal to a contest of sacrifice?
35064: The contest took place on Mount Carmel; fire fell on Elijah's sacrifice.
35065: Where did King Saul and his son Jonathan die in battle with the Philistines?
35067: Saul's sons were killed and Saul fell on his own sword on Mount Gilboa.
35068: In which city were the disciples first called "Christians"?
35070: Barnabas and Saul taught at Antioch for a year, and there the disciples were first called Christians.
35071: In which city did Paul speak at the Areopagus about an altar "to an unknown god"?
35074: Paul addressed the Areopagus in Athens, starting from an altar inscription.
35075: Near which city did Jesus ask "Who do you say that I am?" and Peter confess him as the Christ (in Matthew and Mark)?
35077: Matthew and Mark place the confession in the district of Caesarea Philippi, near the sources of the Jordan.
35078: On which island was John when he received the visions of Revelation?
35080: John says he was on the island called Patmos on account of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.
35081: On which island was Paul shipwrecked on his way to Rome?
35082: After two weeks adrift the ship ran aground on Malta, where Paul survived a viper bite and healed Publius' father.
35083: Abram's family set out for Canaan from which city of the Chaldeans?
35085: Terah took Abram, Sarai and Lot from Ur of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran on the way to Canaan.
35086: Jonah boarded a ship at Joppa to flee to which destination?
35088: Jonah went the opposite way from Nineveh, heading for Tarshish, usually located in the far west Mediterranean.
35089: Where did Jacob dream of a stairway reaching to heaven?
35092: Jacob named the place Bethel, "house of God." Peniel is where he later wrestled with God.
35093: In which town did Jesus raise a widow's only son during his funeral procession?
35094: Only Luke records the raising of the widow's son at the gate of Nain. Lazarus was raised at Bethany.
35096: Which Old Testament book never explicitly names God in its Hebrew text?
35097: Esther never names God, though many see his providence in its events, as in Mordecai's "relief and deliverance will rise from another place."
35098: Which is the longest psalm, an extended acrostic meditation on God's word?
35099: Psalm 119 has 176 verses: 22 stanzas of 8 lines, one for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet.
35100: Which New Testament letter is addressed to a believer about his slave Onesimus?
35101: Paul appeals to Philemon to receive Onesimus "no longer as a slave but more than a slave, as a beloved brother."
35102: Which Gospel opens with "In the beginning was the Word"?
35103: John's prologue echoes Genesis 1:1 and identifies the Word who became flesh.
35104: Which New Testament books are both addressed to Theophilus?
35109: Both open by addressing Theophilus, and Acts refers back to "the first book."
35110: Which book is a series of mostly acrostic poems mourning the destruction of Jerusalem?
35111: Chapters 1-4 of Lamentations are alphabetic acrostics; chapter 5 has 22 lines but is not an acrostic.
35112: Which is the shortest book of the Old Testament by number of verses?
35113: Obadiah has 21 verses in one chapter.
35114: Which book contains the chapter often called the "hall of faith," listing Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham and others?
35115: Hebrews 11 recounts what the faithful did "by faith."
35116: Which prophetic book contains the vision of a valley of dry bones coming to life?
35117: Ezekiel 37 pictures Israel's national restoration as bones receiving flesh and breath.
35118: Which chapter of 1 Corinthians is the famous description of love that is patient and kind?
35119: Chapter 13 sits between Paul's discussions of spiritual gifts in chapters 12 and 14.
35120: Which letter argues that "faith apart from works is dead"?
35121: James insists genuine faith shows itself in action, using Abraham and Rahab as examples.
35122: In the traditional order of the Hebrew Bible (Tanakh), which book comes last?
35124: The Tanakh ends with Chronicles, closing on Cyrus' decree to rebuild the temple. Christian Old Testaments, following the Greek order, end with Malachi.
35126: Around when did the northern kingdom of Israel fall to Assyria?
35131: Samaria fell after a three-year siege, conventionally dated 722 (or 721) BC.
35132: Around when did Babylon destroy Jerusalem and Solomon's temple?
35135: Most date the fall to 586 BC, though some argue for 587 BC.
35136: Around when did the united kingdom split into Israel and Judah after Solomon?
35140: The division followed Solomon's death and Rehoboam's harsh answer to the northern tribes; common chronologies place it about 931/930 BC.
35141: In what year did Cyrus of Persia capture Babylon, opening the way for exiles to return?
35146: Babylon fell to the Persians in 539 BC; Cyrus' decree followed in his first year over Babylon.
35147: When was the second temple completed?
35149: About 516/515 BC, in the sixth year of Darius
35152: Ezra says it was finished in the sixth year of Darius I. Herod later expanded it massively from about 20 BC.
35158: Whether dated early (about 1446 BC) or late (about 1260 BC), the exodus precedes the monarchy, the exile and the return.
35159: In what year did the Romans destroy the Jerusalem temple, as Jesus had foretold?
35162: Roman forces under Titus destroyed the temple in AD 70. Jesus had said not one stone would be left on another.
35163: Herod the Great is usually thought to have died about 4 BC. What does that imply about Jesus' birth?
35164: It probably happened a few years before AD 1
35166: It came several years after Herod's death
35167: It must have been after AD 6
35168: Matthew places Jesus' birth during Herod's reign. The AD system was calculated centuries later and is slightly off; a minority dates Herod's death to 1 BC.
35169: Nehemiah came to Jerusalem in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes I. About when was that?
35173: The twentieth year of Artaxerxes I falls around 445/444 BC.
35174: Which of these prophets ministered earliest?
35175: Elijah was active in the 9th century BC under Ahab; Isaiah in the 8th, Jeremiah in the 7th-6th, Malachi in the 5th.
35177: Which prophet was among the herdsmen of Tekoa?
35178: Amos, from Tekoa in Judah, was sent to prophesy to the northern kingdom.
35179: Which prophet was told to marry Gomer as a sign of Israel's unfaithfulness?
35180: Hosea's marriage to Gomer pictured God's relationship with unfaithful Israel.
35181: Who saw the Lord high and lifted up "in the year that King Uzziah died"?
35182: Isaiah's temple vision includes the seraphim crying "Holy, holy, holy" and his commission.
35183: Which prophet was commanded not to take a wife or have children, as a sign of coming disaster?
35184: Jeremiah's celibacy signalled that families in Judah would perish.
35185: Which prophet was told not to mourn openly when his wife died, as a sign to the exiles?
35186: God called Ezekiel's wife "the delight of your eyes"; his restrained grief prefigured the people's reaction to the temple's fall.
35187: Who asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit?
35188: Elisha asked for the firstborn's share of Elijah's spirit and took up his mantle.
35189: Which prophetic book is entirely an oracle against Edom?
35190: Obadiah condemns Edom for gloating over Jerusalem's fall. Nahum is directed against Nineveh.
35191: Which prophet foretold that a ruler would come from Bethlehem Ephrathah?
35192: The chief priests cite Micah to Herod when the magi ask where the Messiah is to be born.
35193: Which prophet's promise of the Spirit poured out on all flesh does Peter quote at Pentecost?
35194: Peter says the Pentecost events are "what was uttered through the prophet Joel."
35195: Which prophetess did King Josiah's officials consult about the newly found Book of the Law?
35197: Huldah confirmed the book's warnings but promised Josiah would die before the disaster. Noadiah opposed Nehemiah; Anna appears in Luke.
35199: Who was the first king of Israel?
35200: Samuel anointed Saul of the tribe of Benjamin as the first king.
35201: Which queen seized the throne of Judah and tried to destroy the royal family?
35202: Athaliah, daughter of Ahab, ruled about six years until the hidden boy Joash was crowned.
35203: Which king led a sweeping reform after the Book of the Law was found in the temple?
35204: Josiah tore his clothes on hearing the book read and renewed the covenant.
35205: Which king set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan?
35206: Jeroboam feared his people would return to Jerusalem to worship, so he built rival shrines.
35207: Which king of Judah was struck with a skin disease for burning incense in the temple?
35208: Uzziah grew proud and usurped a priestly duty; he lived in isolation until he died.
35209: Which king spread Sennacherib's threatening letter before the LORD and saw Jerusalem delivered?
35210: Hezekiah prayed in the temple; Isaiah brought God's answer, and the Assyrian army was struck down.
35211: Which king of Judah reigned 55 years and, according to Chronicles, repented in captivity?
35212: Kings records Manasseh's long and wicked reign; Chronicles adds his humbling in Babylon and restoration.
35213: Which army commander was anointed king of Israel at Elisha's instruction and destroyed Ahab's dynasty?
35216: A young prophet sent by Elisha anointed Jehu at Ramoth-gilead.
35217: Which foreign king does Isaiah call the LORD's "anointed"?
35220: Isaiah names Cyrus as the one God would use to rebuild Jerusalem and free the exiles.
35221: What was the result of Rehoboam's harsh reply to the northern tribes?
35224: The northern tribes rejected him and made Jeroboam king
35226: Following younger advisers, Rehoboam threatened heavier burdens; ten tribes broke away.
35228: Who was chosen by lot to replace Judas among the Twelve?
35230: Two candidates were put forward; the lot fell on Matthias.
35231: Which of the Twelve is the first whose death Acts records?
35232: Herod Agrippa I killed James with the sword. Stephen died earlier but was not one of the Twelve.
35233: Which brothers did Jesus nickname "Boanerges," sons of thunder?
35238: Mark records the nickname in the list of the Twelve.
35239: In John's Gospel, who first brought his brother Simon to Jesus?
35240: Andrew told Simon, "We have found the Messiah," and brought him to Jesus.
35241: Who told Nathanael about Jesus and answered his doubts with "Come and see"?
35242: Nathanael asked whether anything good could come from Nazareth; Philip replied, "Come and see."
35243: In Galatians, Paul says Peter was entrusted with the gospel to the circumcised and he with the gospel to whom?
35247: James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship for the Gentile mission.
35248: Which of the Twelve was a tax collector when Jesus called him?
35249: Matthew's Gospel calls him "Matthew the tax collector"; Mark and Luke call him Levi.
35250: Who does Paul greet with Andronicus as "of note among the apostles," a phrase whose meaning is debated?

35253: Church tradition most commonly identifies the anonymous "disciple whom Jesus loved" as which apostle?
35254: The Gospel never names him. Second-century tradition identifies him with John; some modern scholars propose other candidates.
35255: Who was the man the apostles called Barnabas, "son of encouragement"?
35260: Barnabas sold a field and gave the money to the apostles. John Mark was his cousin.
35262: The Council of Nicaea (AD 325) was called chiefly to address which controversy?
35263: Pelagianism, about grace and free will
35264: Arianism, whether the Son is fully divine
35267: Nicaea affirmed that the Son is "of one substance" (homoousios) with the Father against Arius. It also dealt with the date of Easter and other matters.
35268: Which emperor, together with Licinius, agreed in 313 to grant Christians legal toleration (the "Edict of Milan")?
35271: Constantine and Licinius agreed on religious toleration in 313. Diocletian had led the Great Persecution; Theodosius later made Nicene Christianity the state religion.
35272: In which town did Martin Luther publish his Ninety-five Theses in 1517?
35275: Luther was a professor at Wittenberg. Geneva was Calvin's city, Zurich Zwingli's, and Worms the site of the 1521 diet.
35276: Augustine served as bishop of which North African city?
35278: Augustine was converted in Milan, influenced by Ambrose, and became bishop of Hippo Regius. His *Confessions* describes reading Romans 13 at his conversion.
35279: Irenaeus of Lyon wrote *Against Heresies* chiefly to refute which teaching?
35284: Irenaeus (late 2nd century) opposed Gnostic systems such as Valentinianism, appealing to apostolic tradition and the goodness of creation. The other movements arose later.
35285: What did the Council of Chalcedon (AD 451) define about Christ?
35286: One person in two natures, without confusion, change, division or separation
35287: One nature, the divine absorbing the human
35288: Two persons joined by moral union
35289: A man adopted as Son at his baptism
35290: Chalcedon's definition became the standard for Catholic, Orthodox and most Protestant churches; the Oriental Orthodox churches did not accept it.
35291: What is the central claim of Peter's Pentecost sermon?
35292: The temple must be rebuilt for the Messiah
35293: Jesus was a prophet who will return as Elijah
35294: Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved
35295: God raised the crucified Jesus and made him Lord and Christ
35296: Peter argues from Joel and the Psalms that the risen and exalted Jesus has poured out the Spirit.
35297: Who produced the Latin translation of the Bible later known as the Vulgate?
35299: Jerome worked in the late 4th and early 5th centuries, translating much of the Old Testament directly from Hebrew.
35300: The split between Eastern and Western churches is conventionally dated to which year?
35301: Mutual excommunications in 1054 symbolise a separation that developed over centuries.
35302: Who produced the first printed English New Testament translated from the Greek?
35306: Tyndale's New Testament was printed in 1526; he was executed in 1536. Wycliffite Bibles were earlier but handwritten and translated from Latin.
35308: What does amillennialism hold about the thousand years of Revelation 20?
35309: They symbolise Christ's present reign between his first and second comings
35310: Christ returns before a future thousand-year reign on earth
35311: Christ returns after the gospel brings an extended era of flourishing
35312: The thousand years were fulfilled entirely in AD 70
35313: Amillennialists read Revelation 20 as describing the current age, with Satan bound so the gospel can go to the nations.
35315: Christ will return before a future reign on earth, the millennium
35316: The millennium is the present church age
35317: Christ returns after a golden age of gospel success
35318: There will be no future resurrection of the body
35319: Premillennialists, historic and dispensational, read Revelation 20 as following Christ's return in Revelation 19.
35321: Christ returns after an extended era in which the gospel transforms much of the world
35322: Christ returns before a literal thousand-year reign
35324: The world will steadily worsen until a secret rapture
35325: Postmillennialists draw on the growth parables and the Great Commission to expect widespread gospel success before Christ comes.
35326: What does the penal substitution view of the atonement hold?
35327: Christ's death chiefly defeats the powers of sin, death and the devil
35328: Christ's death chiefly reveals God's love to move us to repentance
35329: Christ bore the penalty of sin in the place of sinners
35330: Christ's death restored God's offended honour by satisfaction

35333: Christ's death and resurrection defeat sin, death and the devil
35334: Christ pays a legal penalty owed to divine justice
35336: Christ restores God's honour as a feudal lord
35337: Associated with early church writers and revived by Gustaf Aulen, it highlights Christ triumphing over the powers.
35338: What does conditional immortality (annihilationism) hold about the final state of the lost?
35340: All will eventually be reconciled to God
35341: They are ultimately destroyed and cease to exist
35342: They are reincarnated for another chance
35343: Proponents argue immortality is God's gift to the redeemed and read "destroy" and "perish" literally.
35344: What does the credobaptist view hold?
35345: The infant children of believers should be baptised
35346: Baptism is for those who personally profess faith in Christ
35347: Baptism is unnecessary because it is purely inward
35348: Only those baptised by an apostle are truly baptised
35349: Credobaptists point to the pattern of belief then baptism in Acts.
35350: What does the paedobaptist view hold?
35351: Only adults who profess faith may be baptised
35352: Children of believers should be baptised as members of the covenant community
35353: Baptism should be delayed until death

35356: What does complementarianism hold about men and women?

35358: All roles in church and home are open to both on the basis of gifting
35359: Women are less in the image of God than men
35360: Women may not take any part in church ministry

35363: Certain leadership roles are reserved for qualified men
35364: Men and women are identical with no differences
35365: All ministries and leadership roles are open to women and men on the basis of gifting and calling
35366: Leadership belongs only to unmarried believers
35367: Egalitarians point to women prophets, co-workers and mutual submission. The claim that they deny all differences between the sexes is a straw man.
35368: What does cessationism hold about spiritual gifts?

35370: Certain miraculous and revelatory gifts ceased after the apostolic era
35371: No spiritual gifts were ever miraculous
35372: Gifts are given only to ordained clergy

35375: Why was the Samaritan woman surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink?

35381: In Jesus' parable of the vineyard labourers, a denarius represents what?
35385: A typical day's wage for a labourer
35386: The owner agrees with workers for a denarius a day.
35387: What did the feast of Passover commemorate?
35388: The giving of the law at Sinai
35389: God's deliverance of Israel from Egypt
35392: Passover remembers the night the LORD passed over Israel's houses and struck Egypt's firstborn. Purim celebrates the victory over Haman.
35393: Why did Israelites live in temporary shelters during the Feast of Booths (Tabernacles)?
35394: To mourn the destruction of the temple
35395: To prepare for the barley harvest
35396: To remember that God made Israel live in booths after the exodus
35397: To honour the patriarchs' tents in Canaan
35398: Leviticus explains the booths as a reminder of the wilderness journey.
35399: Which group denied the resurrection of the dead?
35402: Acts says the Sadducees say there is no resurrection, angel or spirit, while the Pharisees acknowledge them.
35407: The chief Jewish council in Jerusalem, presided over by the high priest

35416: Read the whole law to the people
35418: Enter the Most Holy Place with blood once a year
35419: Offer the first sheaf of barley
